public.prompt: Several same-origin tabs show an order draft and exchange server-accepted incremental patches through `BroadcastChannel`. Each patch has a strictly increasing revision and is valid only on the immediately preceding revision; a canonical full snapshot can be fetched. Delays can expose an older patch after a newer one or leave a revision gap. Which reconciliation policy prevents corruption?

options.label: Apply every arriving patch immediately because channel delivery order is the freshest sequence shared by the tabs.
Sort patches by sender timestamps, apply the latest clock value, and replace server revisions when local time is newer.
Apply the next contiguous server revision, ignore older revisions, and refetch a snapshot for a missing intermediate patch.

answerProof.summary: The server revision is the shared monotonic authority. A patch can be applied only to its declared predecessor; older revisions are stale, while a forward gap requires the canonical snapshot instead of applying an incomplete transition.
decisiveConstraints: Each patch depends on the immediately preceding server revision.
Message arrival order may differ from accepted change order.
All tabs share the same server-issued revision sequence.
The full snapshot is the authoritative recovery path for a missing patch.

claims.statement: BroadcastChannel provides same-origin cross-context messaging, but the application defines the message protocol and reconciliation meaning.

optionRationales.explanation: Arrival order can lag or skip the server sequence, so applying a stale or noncontiguous patch can regress or corrupt the draft.
optionRationales.plausibility: Within one ordered producer, processing patches as received can be a simple transition policy.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: A patch may run only on the server revision it names as its predecessor.

optionRationales.explanation: Client clocks can skew and do not prove that every prerequisite server patch has been applied.
optionRationales.plausibility: Wall-clock timestamps are easy to attach and appear to provide a total ordering for user edits.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: The server revision is the only monotonic ordering shared by every participant.

optionRationales.explanation: Contiguous revisions preserve patch preconditions, stale revisions lose authority, and snapshot recovery closes an unreconstructable gap.
